acceptance_criteria.given: a scratch project with a capability and a change whose requirement has accepted evidence and a landed task
acceptance_criteria.how_to_check: py -3.11 scripts/drive/d1015_f593_fold_keeps_verification.py <project> (written first: fails before the build)
acceptance_criteria.then: the capability's folded requirement is verified, naming the change requirement as served_by
acceptance_criteria.when: the operator folds the change into the capability and reads the project's coverage

acceptance_criteria.then: the project totals count the requirement once; the change's own coverage still lists it
acceptance_criteria.when: the operator reads the project's coverage and the archived change's own

acceptance_criteria.then: only the unchanged one inherits; one with its own evidence keeps its own
acceptance_criteria.when: coverage is computed for a reworded folded requirement and an unchanged one

design: Tier 1, no migration. D1. The link is what the Hub already records: spec_document_merges (capability <- change) plus the semantic digest, which covers modal, statement, party and criteria and not the identifier, so a requirement folded verbatim keeps its digest. A reworded fold changes the digest and inherits nothing, which is right: the old evidence demonstrated other words. D2. Inherited only when the capability requirement has no evidence of its own; its own evidence, once recorded, governs. D3. Rejected: copying accepted evidence at fold (doubles counts, and F-rules refuse duplicate evidence per commit). D4. The project rollup filters on document phase; document_id-scoped reads are unchanged, so the archived change's page still reads its history.

checked: requirement_coverage has no phase filter and reads evidence by requirement_id only
spec_digest.semantic_digest takes modal, statement, party and criteria, not the identifier
spec_document_merges records capability_document_id and change_document_id per fold
limits: A capability requirement folded from two changes with the same digest names the first found

problem: Folding a verified change into its capability listed the capability's new requirements as unserved with no evidence, while the archived change kept counting as verified in the project totals: coverage said the shipped behaviour was unserved and counted history as verified (sweeps of 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-15, through the API and on screen).

requirements.rationale: The fold carries the requirement's text unchanged; what demonstrated it still demonstrates it.
requirements.statement: A capability requirement with no evidence of its own SHALL take its coverage state and integration from the requirement of a change merged into that capability that carries the same digest, and its coverage entry SHALL name that requirement as served_by.

requirements.rationale: An archived change is history; counting it beside the capability that holds its requirements counts them twice.
requirements.statement: The project's coverage rollup SHALL leave out the requirements of archived documents; a document's own coverage SHALL still list them.

in_scope: requirement_coverage: a capability requirement with no evidence of its own is served by the same-digest requirement of a change merged into it
requirement_coverage: the project rollup leaves out requirements of archived documents
non_goals: Copying evidence rows into the capability (it would double every count)
The app showing which change serves a requirement (the UI batch)
Re-verifying a capability requirement a later commit broke (drift's job)

summary: After a fold, a capability requirement folded unchanged from a verified change reads verified, naming the change requirement that serves it; the project's coverage rollup leaves archived documents out of its totals (F593).

tasks.title: Coverage reads a folded requirement's verification and leaves archived documents out of the rollup

title: A folded requirement keeps the verification it earned
